Shares key_limits_block with the mint and /resend-verify, so the three

post.description:
Re-send the confirmation link for this key's email address.

Exists so an agent that hits the unverified daily cap can get its human back
on track without leaving the session — the 429 body names this endpoint. The
10-minute resend cooldown inside _issue_verify is the abuse floor.

Only ever acts on the CALLER'S OWN key, so the outcome is reported honestly
rather than blurred: there is no other account's state to probe here, and a
vague "sent" for a mail that never went out just sends an agent back to wait
for an email that will never arrive.

Full dual-score market health result with all 11 components.

**`indicators` contract**

Top-level `indicators` is a flat denormalization of the most-filtered values
from `components.<x>.details`. Keys are **omitted entirely** when the source
value is unavailable (never null) so consumers can safely use
`dict.get(key, default)` for fallbacks. Committed key set:

- `long_short_ratio` (float) — BTC long/short ratio (Binance perps)
- `funding_rate` (float, %) — avg funding rate (aliased from `avg_funding_rate`)
- `buy_ratio` (float, 0–1) — weighted taker-buy ratio across top spot pairs
- `fear_greed_value` (int, 0–100) — averaged Fear & Greed index
- `breadth_pct` (float, %) — share of top-30 coins above their 200D MA
- `pct_from_200ma` (float, %) — BTC distance from 200D MA
- `cross_status` (str) — Golden | Death | Neutral
- `stablecoin_change_7d` (float) — 7-day stablecoin market-cap change

Health is computed cross-exchange (CoinGlass aggregate + Binance) and is not
scoped by any per-exchange filter. The `long_short_ratio` is BTC-on-Binance,
used as a market-wide sentiment signal.
Scores + sentiment only (lightweight).

get.description:
One indicator in full: definition summary, strategies that use it, the
CDA endpoints behind it, its AlgoBrain page path and an AI-agent prompt.

SIGNUM_RGG trend radar across all live Hyperliquid perps + liquid Binance USDT pairs.

Each asset gets a daily RED/GREY/GREEN color from ADX(14)+DMI with hysteresis,
plus days-in-color, flip date, % change since flip, and (for grey) the 20-day
consolidation range. Recomputed hourly (:05 UTC).

**Bar contract:** ``color`` / ``days_in_color`` / ``adx`` / ``flipped_at`` /
``price`` are read from **completed** daily bars (``computed_from`` = the
last completed UTC day, ``is_final: true``). ``color_live`` / ``adx_live`` /
``days_in_color_live`` include the forming UTC bar and can change intraday.

**flip_alert** is true when the last 4 closed 1h bars ALL carry a colour
different from the daily ``color`` (``intraday_disagrees`` is the same
value; ``flip_alert_reason`` names it). ``recent_flip`` = ``days_in_color
<= 3``. ``intraday_timeframe`` is always ``"1h"``.

**pegged** rows (stablecoins, $1-pinned tokens) stay in the list but are
excluded from every breadth aggregate and top list on ``/daily``.

Universe: Hyperliquid wins the dedupe on overlap; Binance spot fills the
gaps (pairs with >=$100k 24h quote volume). ``universe_size`` is the full
row count before filters; page with ``offset`` + ``limit`` (max 1000).

``symbol`` (alias ``coin``) narrows to a comma list of assets; any it names that the
universe does not cover come back in ``not_covered``. Per-interval ADX numbers (1d, 4h,
1h) for the same rows are ``/indicators/adx``. An unrecognised query parameter is a 400.

get.description:
ADX(14) + DMI per asset on daily, 4h or 1h bars (Pro tier).

The same Wilder ADX/+DI/-DI the SIGNUM trend radar colours from, served as numbers per
interval: ``interval=1d`` matches ``/indicators/signum-rgg`` ``adx``, ``4h`` its
``h4_adx`` (completed bars on the UTC 00/04/08/12/16/20 grid of
``/hyperliquid/candles?interval=4h``) and ``1h`` its ``intraday_adx``. Recomputed hourly
(:05 UTC) for the whole universe, so a universe-wide read costs nothing.

Per row: ``adx``, ``plus_di``, ``minus_di``; ``direction`` (+DI vs -DI); ``strength``
against SIGNUM's bands (``strong`` >= 25, ``weak`` < 20); ``color`` (the SIGNUM state on
that interval); ``bar_open`` and ``final``. A row whose interval read is unavailable
(too few bars, or a stale intraday series) carries nulls and sorts last.

``history=N`` attaches the last N completed bars per row. For 4h and 1h that is a live
candle pull per symbol (memoised 30 minutes), so it needs ``coin`` with at most 5
symbols. An unrecognised query parameter is a 400.

Example gates: ``?coin=BTC&interval=4h`` -> ``items[0].adx > 25``;
``?interval=1d&min_adx=25&source=hyperliquid_perp`` -> every trending HL perp.

get.description:
Technical / Structural regime overlay (Regime #14, Pro tier).

Per-asset price-structure state across the same universe as SIGNUM_RGG:
moving-average position (SMA-50/100/200 + last cross), Bollinger-band
squeeze + bandwidth percentile, 20d range position, RSI(14) extremes on
daily + 1h timeframes, and `sr` — up to 3 support + 3 resistance levels
per side, from swing-high/low pivots on the daily series, nearest to
current price first. A level's `strength` is how many pivots clustered
into it; `dist_pct` is its signed % distance from mark (negative =
support, positive = resistance). Levels further than 30% from mark are
dropped as not actionable.

``breadth`` reports compression breadth over the FULL universe regardless
of filters: ``{total, in_squeeze, pct_in_squeeze,
pct_in_squeeze_pctile_30d, history_days}`` — the percentile ranks today's
squeeze share against the last 30 archived daily values (null until 10
days are archived).

Filter via `ma_state`, `bb`, `range_zone`, `rsi` (each is optional and
AND-combined). Example screener queries:

  - `?bb=in_squeeze&sort=squeeze_days&order=desc` — assets compressed for longest
  - `?rsi=oversold&min_days_in_state=2` — sustained oversold candidates
  - `?ma_state=reclaim_200` — recent 200MA reclaims (last 10 days)
  - `?range_zone=near_high&ma_state=above_200` — near-range-high + uptrend
  - `?symbol=BTC,ETH,SOL` — just those assets (alias `coin`); any the universe does not
    cover are listed in `not_covered`

Every series is DAILY (``ma`` carries SMA-20/50/100/200). An unrecognised query parameter
(``interval``, say) is a 400, not a silently ignored filter; 4h / 1h ADX is
``/indicators/adx``.

get.description:
One-call scan table for a coin universe (Pro) — what otherwise takes one call per coin.

Each row joins the SIGNUM_RGG daily colour (``signum``, ``days_in_color``, ``adx``),
rolling hourly moves (``pct_1h``, ``pct_4h``, ``pct_24h``), 30-day notional liquidity
(``notional_30`` — mean daily USD volume, the same field as ``/volatility/regime``
``vol.notional_30``) and the daily 200-SMA position (``above_sma200``,
``dist_from_200_pct`` — from ``/indicators/technical``). Served from data the API already
holds, so the whole universe is one instant call and spends no exchange rate limit.

**The moves are rolling windows over COMPLETED hourly bars.** ``pct_4h`` is the change from
the close four hours before the last completed hourly close to that close — it is NOT the
open-to-close of a 4h bar, so it is not aligned to 00/04/08 UTC. ``as_of`` is the close
time of that last completed bar. They refresh hourly (:05 UTC) with SIGNUM_RGG, so during
the hour they describe the last full hour, not the forming one. ``price`` is that bar's
close. A window whose bar is missing from the series is ``null``. ``pct_4h_bar`` IS the
clock-aligned move: open to close of the last closed UTC 4h bar, ending at
``bar_4h_as_of``. The top-level ``moves`` object states this in every response.

``signum`` / ``days_in_color`` / ``adx`` are the completed-DAILY read, the same bar
contract as ``/indicators/signum-rgg``. ``signum_4h`` / ``bars_in_color_4h`` are the same
cascade over COMPLETED 4h bars on the ``/hyperliquid/candles?interval=4h`` grid (null when
under 30 complete 4h bars). Pegged / stablecoin rows are excluded.

Filters: ``min_notional_30`` (liquidity floor), ``color``, ``color_4h``, ``above_sma200``. Sort with
``sort`` (default ``notional_30``); ``sort=pct`` orders by the move named by ``interval``.
Rows lacking the sort value go last. ``source`` defaults to ``hyperliquid_perp``.

Example: ``?min_notional_30=3000000&color=green&above_sma200=true&sort=pct&interval=4h``.

get.description:
Open interest across all Hyperliquid assets.

``as_of`` (ms) is when the ``metaAndAssetCtxs`` snapshot behind every row
was fetched (60s cadence); ``generated_at`` (ms) is when this response was
built. ``open_interest_usd = open_interest x mark_price``; ``premium`` is
HL's own context field. ``coverage`` explains the row count: HL keeps
delisted perps in its universe and they are excluded here.

Trailing OHLCV candles for up to 25 coins in ONE call — the same bars
``/hyperliquid/candles`` serves per coin, keyed by coin under ``series``.

Trailing ``limit`` only; for an explicit ``start``/``end`` range use the
single-coin route. Every coin must be in HL's universe (400 ``unknown_coin``
otherwise — nothing is silently dropped). On a cold cache a series that has
not arrived within ~8s is listed in ``pending`` instead of holding the
whole response, and ``retry_after_s`` says how long to wait (scaled to how many
are still fetching): their fetches keep running and are cached, so retry just
the ``pending`` coins after that. A cold coin costs Hyperliquid rate limit
(~20 weight, whatever ``limit`` is), so a first pull of many coins takes a
while and repeat pulls are instant; for a whole-universe scan that needs no
candles at all, use ``/indicators/heatmap``. ``atr`` and
``forming_bar_timestamp`` behave as on ``/hyperliquid/candles``.

The contract: ``complete`` is true iff every requested coin is in ``series``; a
coin is never in both ``series`` and ``pending``. ``wait`` (0-25s, default 8)
holds longer for a caller that prefers one call over a poll. ``closed_only=true``
returns the last ``limit`` COMPLETED bars — the read for a strategy that acts on a
closed bar — and is served from any series fetched since the latest close, so the
liquid coins pre-warmed just after each 4h close stay instant for the whole bar.
Fees for sizing are on ``/hyperliquid/meta`` (``fees``); funding + OI on the same
bar grid are ``/backtesting/hl-funding-bars`` (join on ``timestamp``).

get.description:
OHLCV candles for a coin — trailing ``limit`` bars, or an explicit range.

**These are Hyperliquid's own bars** (``candleSnapshot``) — the execution
truth for an HL book: signal, size and mark a Hyperliquid position from this
series. ``/api/v1/backtesting/klines`` is our archive of the same venue's 1m
bars for deep history, not a second price source. For several coins at once
use ``/hyperliquid/candles/batch``.

``coin`` is HL's own name, matched case-insensitively (``symbol`` is accepted
as an alias, and a ``USDT`` / ``-PERP`` suffix is tolerated). A name HL does
not list is a 400 ``unknown_coin`` and an unrecognised query parameter a 400
``unknown_parameter`` — never a silent default-coin reply.

``atr=14`` adds a Wilder ATR to every bar (``atr``; null for the first
``atr`` bars) computed on this exact series, so every agent uses the same
number. The LAST bar is usually still forming: ``forming_bar_timestamp``
names it (null when the last bar has closed) — drop it, and its ``atr``,
for completed-bar signals.

Pass ``start`` (and optionally ``end``) as epoch milliseconds or ISO-8601
to fetch a fixed window instead of the trailing ``limit``; ranges longer
than one candleSnapshot page are paginated, up to **15,000 bars** per call
(400 above that — narrow the window or step the interval up). Explicit
ranges bypass the 60s response cache and spend live HL weight (20 per
1,500-bar page), so poll them sparingly.

**Retention is Hyperliquid's, not ours:** HL serves roughly 4 days of 1m
bars and progressively more at coarser intervals; a ``start`` older than
that simply returns fewer bars. For multi-month 1m history use
``/api/v1/backtesting/klines?exchange=hyperliquid&start=&end=`` (our own
archive since 2026-03-30).

``start`` / ``end`` in the response echo the resolved window (ms) for a
range request and are null for a trailing pull.

Every row is one closed UTC minute. ``buy_notional`` / ``sell_notional``

replay. A covered minute with no fills is a genuine zero (``0.0``,
``partial: false``). ``stream.coverage_pct`` is the share of the last 60
minutes fully watched.

``trade_flow_warming`` until the first bucket closes (about a minute
after the collector starts); 404 for a coin HL does not list. Pro.

get.description:
Search the AlgoBrain strategy wiki (~5k pages: strategies, the Hyperliquid
signal baskets, concepts, methodology).

**Ranking** (2026-10-10): a page NAMED by the query comes first (its title, an acronym in
its title, or an alias), then pages with the whole query as a phrase in their title or
aliases, then every term in the title/aliases, then every term anywhere, then any term.
Within each tier, concept and strategy pages rank above the ~2.5k generated per-coin
pages, then by BM25. Each result says which tier it came from in ``match``
(``exact_title``, ``title_phrase``, ``title_terms``, ``all_terms``, ``any_term``); its
``score`` (BM25) orders results only within a tier.

Each result carries ``path``, ``title``, ``type``, ``tags``, a ``snippet``
around the match, a relevance ``score`` (higher is better; null when ``q`` is
empty) and ``read`` — the ``/algobrain/page`` URL for the full markdown. Filters
without ``q`` list matching pages by title. A bare call (no ``q``, no filter) lists
the newest pages by their ``updated`` date, so an agent can discover real paths
before it has a query. All tiers. Content is CC BY 4.0.

Strategy pages also carry ``strategy``: the authors' frontmatter —
``backtest_status``, ``horizon``, ``strategy_type``, ``complexity``,
``crowding_risk``, ``markets``, ``edge_source`` and the ESTIMATES
``expected_sharpe`` / ``expected_max_drawdown`` / ``breakeven_cost_bps``, labelled
``expected_sharpe_source: "author_estimate"``. They are literature expectations, not
results measured on any venue, so results are never ranked by them; filter on
``backtest_status`` (e.g. ``cost-corrected``, ``walk-forward-validated``, ``live``)
to find the pages with the most evidence behind them. ``strategy`` is null on
non-strategy pages. Each strategy filter is an any-of match (``horizon=swing``
also finds ``swing|position`` pages).

``strategy.runnable`` / ``strategy.gate_counts`` summarise the page's **gates** — each
condition the strategy checks mapped to one endpoint and one response field, or marked
partial (a human judgement remains) or not runnable (we serve nothing that measures it).
``runnable=all`` finds pages an agent can run end to end. The gates themselves are on
``/algobrain/page``. An unrecognised query parameter is a 400.

get.description:
Dealer positioning / Gamma Exposure — perp analog (Pro).

Built from **market-maker** accounts (the perp "dealers"): per coin we report
`mm_net_delta` (dealer inventory long/short), `gamma_profile` (the MM
liquidation-density by price = where MM forced unwinds cluster, the
short-gamma acceleration zones) and `gamma_flip` (the price where MM
long-liq-below crosses short-liq-above — the inflection).

Note: perps have no literal options gamma; this is a behavioral analog from
market-maker inventory + liquidation-driven forced flow, not options dealer
gamma. The MM set is a heuristic classification (turnover + breadth + known
desks), so treat it as a positioning signal, not an exact dealer book.

Each coin also carries the composite **`regime`** flag — `amplify`
(short-gamma analog: crowded book + dense clusters near mark → forced flow
follows through) vs `dampen` (balanced, mean-reverting) vs `transitional`
(on the flip line) — joining the cluster profile with funding skew, OI
rate-of-change, the realized-liquidation cascade signal and the
`dist_to_flip_pct`. Every sub-signal is returned in `regime.inputs` so the
call is reproducible. `meta.maintenance_margin_tiers` gives the per-pair MM /
max-leverage ladder for context.

**`distribution_context`** (per coin) puts today's readings in
distributional context: trailing-30-day percentile ranks of the near-mark
cluster density, |distance to flip|, normalized MM skew
(`mm_net_delta/mm_gross`), regime score and funding rate — e.g. "BTC
near-mark fuel density is the 92nd percentile of 30d". The history is
forward-only (hourly samples, started 2026-07); `history_days` /
`sample_count` report how much exists and every `*_pctile` is null while
`status` is `warming` (< 2 days). `meta.distribution_legend` documents each
field. The same block is archived in the `gamma_exposure` snapshot type.

**2026-09-09 additions.** `regime.coverage` (`full` | `funding_only` |
`none`) + `regime.insufficient_mm_coverage` say how much evidence the state
rests on (118/231 coins carry < 10 MM accounts — a `funding_only` state is a
funding read, not a positioning read); per-coin `coverage {bands,
mm_n_accounts, has_flip, history_days}`. `regime.rules_version` = `"2"`:
the skew leg now scores from `distribution_context.mm_skew_pctile`
(≥90/≤10 one-sided, 25–75 balanced) with the raw `market_skew` rule as the
fallback while a coin's history is `warming` (`regime.inputs.skew_source`
says which). `regime.since` = when the current state was first committed.
`regime.inputs.funding_pinned` flags a funding series glued to HL's 1.25e-5
interest baseline (then `funding_rate_pctile` is null — the rank would be
meaningless). `distribution_context.mm_skew_z` / `sample_ts`. `levels` =
the 3 nearest liquidation clusters above/below mark across EVERY account
class. `positions_as_of` (unix ms) top-level and per coin.
`meta.regime_rules` publishes every threshold and weight;
`meta.classifier_version` the tagging rule-set. `symbol` accepts a comma
list (`BTC,ETH`), alias `coin`, matched case-insensitively against Hyperliquid's
names (`kPEPE`). An unrecognised query parameter is a 400.

`meta.maintenance_margin_tiers` is Hyperliquid's live margin table per coin.

Requires a Pro or Pro Plus key; full-universe (all perps) on both.

get.description:
The 10-state long-horizon regime model + the current detected regime.

``regimes`` is the stable taxonomy (id, machine ``regime`` id, display name,
description, typical duration and directional bias). ``current`` is the live
classification with a ``rationale``, the inspectable ``signals`` that drove
it, and — where applicable — an internal ``stage`` (Distribution) or
``euphoria_score`` (Speculative Euphoria).

**Committed vs live.** ``current.regime``/``id``/``name``/``rationale`` are the
COMMITTED regime: an anti-churn dwell gate holds it until a new candidate is
the raw classification for ``pending.needed`` consecutive refreshes. But
``signals`` are always read fresh, so mid-turn they can stop supporting the
committed regime — that is expected, not stale data. ``current.raw`` gives the
live ungated classification and ``raw.matches_committed`` tells you the two
disagree; ``current.pending`` shows how far the successor has confirmed.

**Stability.** ``pending`` is null whenever the live read already agrees with
the committed regime — correct, but it means a consumer watching for a turn
sees a field that blinks in and out. ``current.stability`` is always present
and always numeric: ``raw_agreement`` decays as conditions drift,
``confirmations_against``/``needed`` track a successor, and ``locked_for_s``
is the HARD number — how long the dwell floor mechanically guarantees the
committed regime survives. ``current.thresholds`` gives the distance from
every numeric cutoff in the cascade to flipping, so hysteresis can be built
on published boundaries instead of guesses.

``typical_duration`` describes the real-world cycle phase, NOT a guaranteed
dwell — but the dwell floor is now SCALED to it: a "Weeks-Months" state
(#2/#4/#6/#8) must be held 48h before anything may replace it, "Weeks" 24h,
"Days-Weeks" 12h, and #1 Structural Shock only 2h because it is an emergency
override. Read the live value from ``stability.dwell_floor_s``.

``/regimes/history`` returns the committed transition sequence.

Committed long-horizon regime transitions over a window (Pro Plus).

``/regimes`` publishes only what is committed right now, so the sequence that
produced it could not be reconstructed from this API at all. Each entry here
is one committed run: which regime, the exact instant it committed, when the
next one replaced it, and how long it held.

**``committed_at`` is exact.** It comes from the ``in_regime_since`` stamped
at commit time and carried in every archived sample — not from the ~25-min
sample that first observed the change. And because every committed regime is
now protected by a minimum-dwell floor of at least 2h, no transition can hide
between two samples.

**Coverage starts 2026-08-07 and cannot be backfilled.** The published regime
is a stateful commit through the anti-churn dwell gate, not a pure function
of the archived signals — replaying older inputs would produce a sequence
that was never actually served. ``coverage_start`` reports the true start.

Not to be confused with ``/quant/regimes/history``, which is the short-horizon
6-state HMM's hourly probability Parquet. This is the 10-state cycle model.

Per-asset realized-volatility regime across the SIGNUM_RGG universe.

Each asset is classified into one of ``vol_shock``, ``expanding``,
``compressed``, ``mean_reverting``, or ``normal`` from realized vol (close-to-
close, Parkinson, Garman-Klass) on daily klines. Each entry carries 7d/30d
vol, the 90d vol percentile, term structure (7d/30d), and a vol-target
position-size multiplier (``target_vol / current_vol``, capped).

**Backfillable** — replayable from daily klines (unlike the intraday-only
liquidity regime). The ``vol.rv_1h`` field is live-only and lands null on
historically backfilled days.

**``vol_target_multiplier`` is ABSOLUTE**: ``60 / rv_gk_30`` (close-to-close
fallback) clamped to ``[0.25, 3.0]`` — not a percentile of the coin's own
history. A coin with 30d vol >= 240% pins at 0.25 for as long as that holds
(``vol.multiplier_at_floor``, ``vol.multiplier_floor_days``). For a
**shock gate use ``vol.rv_z_7 >= 2``** (7d vol two sigmas above its own
trailing 90d) or ``vol_pctile_7``; ``vol_shock`` itself is relative (7d GK
at/above the 90th percentile of the coin's own 90d).

A coin needs ``MIN_BARS`` = 40 daily bars to be classified. Rows whose
candle fetch failed this cycle are carried over from the previous build
(``stale_cycles`` > 0, max 8 cycles) rather than vanishing.

tinder), `?regime=vol_shock` (acute spikes), `?sort=vol_target_multiplier&

the end of the distribution where supply is the story. A coin trading at a
23% float with three times its market cap still locked is a different
instrument from one that is fully distributed.

- `supply_basis` — **which denominator was used**: `max_supply` when the token
  is genuinely capped, else `total_supply`. `max_supply` is absent for over
  half the universe, and "share of max" and "share of total" are different
  claims, so this is stated rather than assumed.

- `dilution_overhang` — locked value as a multiple of current market cap.
- `next_unlock` — the soonest dated cliff, with same-day tranches summed and
  priced (`usd`, `pct_of_float`, `pct_of_market_cap`).
- `unlock_coverage` — `tracked` or `not_tracked`. **A null `next_unlock` with
  `not_tracked` does NOT mean the token has no unlock scheduled**; it means
  no schedule is published for it in our source. Do not read it as "safe".

a nominal `total_supply` rather than a real vesting schedule, and those
artifacts otherwise dominate the top of an ascending-float ranking. Pass
`min_market_cap=0` for the unfiltered set — the rows are still computed, they
are just not what the default board is for.

BTC spot-ETF assets under management (reconstructed estimate).

Returns one row: ``aum_usd_from_flows``, ``btc_held_from_flows``,
``btc_price_usd``, ``cumulative_net_flow_usd``, ``price_appreciation_usd``,

existing stake that never appears here as an inflow, so these cover BTC
accumulated through flows since launch and understate the complex by
roughly that seed. See ``excludes`` in the payload.

This 503'd on EVERY call from the 2026-07-24 CoinGlass retirement until
2026-08-22: CoinGlass was the only AUM feed and no free one exists. It is
derivable though — AUM is coins held times price, and the daily flow history
plus that day's close gives the coins. See
FreeMarketCollector._refresh_etf_aum for the derivation and its biases.

``cumulative_net_flow_usd`` is returned alongside deliberately: it is a
DIFFERENT quantity from AUM (the gap is price appreciation), and conflating
the two is the usual way this number gets misreported.

``flows`` holds SETTLED days only (the full Farside "Total" for that US
trade date), oldest first; ``latest`` is the newest of them. The day still

last — is returned separately as ``in_progress`` (``status: "partial"``,
with how many funds have reported) and never counts toward ``flows``.

issuers had not reported, stamped with the fetch time, so the figure was a
partial sum on most weekdays (23 Sep 2026 BTC read +$32.4M; the settled
Total is +$346.9M).

fills any day Farside has not settled or could not be fetched; each row
names its ``source``. ``source_health`` shows the last success/failure of
each feed. ``xrp`` is not supported (no free source publishes it) and
answers 400.

get.description:
Realized-liquidation data (long/short USD over 1h/4h/12h/24h windows).
Defaults to Hyperliquid perps coins only.

**Coverage:** totals aggregate our configured realized-liquidation venue
feeds (OKX + Bybit + Hyperliquid where armed; the HL contribution is exact
per-fill capture) — see the ``coverage`` field on the response. **Binance,
the largest venue, geo-blocks its liquidation stream from our infrastructure
(no REST fallback), so these figures run below a true all-exchange total.**

**Filter semantics:** ``exchange=`` is a **coin-set filter**, not an
exchange-data filter. With ``exchange=hyperliquid`` you get the coins
listed on Hyperliquid, but the liquidation values inside each entry are the
venue-subset totals above. For Hyperliquid's own per-asset trading data use
``/daily/hyperliquid``.

**AsterDEX coverage:** With ``exchange=asterdex`` the response is the union
of (a) CoinGlass cross-exchange aggregate rows whose symbol is also listed
on AsterDEX and (b) AsterDEX venue-native rows (``source: "asterdex"``)
for AsterDEX-only symbols (e.g. LAB, ASTEROID). Native rows depend on
AsterDEX's force-order feed, which is intermittently disabled upstream;
when unavailable, only the CoinGlass-aggregate rows are returned.

``as_of`` (unix seconds) is when the liquidation snapshot behind ``data``
was last refreshed. Each row also carries ``liq_1h_vs_7d_median``
``{long, short, total, hours_7d}``: the trailing hour's liquidated notional
over the **median hourly notional of the prior 7 days** for that coin
(1.0 = a normal hour), computed from the exact Hyperliquid fill tape on
both sides of the ratio — see ``baseline`` for the exact definition. Null
per side when the 7d median is zero, per row when fewer than 24 hours of
tape exist, and for every row on a box without the backtesting archive.

**Row grain:** each row's USD fields are trailing-window LEVELS (see
``grain``: ``kind: rolling_window``, ``sum_ok: false``) — polling this every
few minutes and summing or differencing the answers double-counts. For
incremental flow use the Pro ``/backtesting/hl-liquidation-bars``, built from
the Hyperliquid fill tape. ``count`` is the number of liquidation events in
the 24h window and ``source`` the venues they came from (``row_count_meaning``).

**Order:** rows are sorted by ``liquidation_usd_24h``, largest first, so
``limit`` keeps the coins with the most liquidated notional. AsterDEX-native
rows (``exchange=asterdex``) follow the aggregate rows.

The free tier is scoped to BTC; full-universe coverage is Pro and Pro Plus.

get.description:
Coins whose forced-liquidation flow is one-sided and abnormal *right now*.

A cascade tripwire, not a news feed. Scored catalysts on
``/news/market-moving`` are 15-45 minutes behind a breaking story — RSS is
polled every 5 minutes and desks publish well after the fact — which is no
use to a leveraged position. This reads the liquidation websocket directly:
on 2026-08-19 the BTC tape printed **$322.8M of short liquidations in one
5-minute bucket at a 334x short/long ratio, 23 minutes before** the first
related headline qualified for the tape.

**`direction` names the side being LIQUIDATED, not the price.** A short
liquidation is the exchange closing a short at market — forced buying — so
`short_squeeze` is upward pressure and `long_flush` is downward, and the
label is correct before price confirms it.

**`oi_state` is what separates the two cases that matter.** Open interest
falling into a short squeeze means shorts are being closed out (the move is
consuming its own fuel); OI rising means fresh positioning is being added
into it. It reads `null` until the OI history has two samples, and `unclear`
inside a ±0.5% noise band rather than being forced into a story.

**Severity is built from ratios**, not dollars: `spike_ratio` (this window
against the coin's own trailing-24h mean) and `asymmetry` (the dominant
side's share) carry 80% of the weight. Absolute notionals are the figure
most distorted by the coverage gap below, so they are weighted least.

**Coverage:** the same venue subset as ``/market-intelligence/liquidations``
(OKX + Bybit + Hyperliquid where armed; Hyperliquid is exact per-fill).
Binance geo-blocks its liquidation stream from our infrastructure, so
notionals run below a true all-exchange total.

**Check `baseline_span_h`, not `window_uptime_h`.** `spike_ratio` compares a
window against a trailing-24h mean, and `baseline_span_h` is how many hours
of history are actually behind that mean — it is what triggering is gated on.
`window_uptime_h` is process uptime and resets on every deploy, while the
feed restores up to 24h of events from its snapshot on boot, so the two
routinely disagree by a full day.

**`triggered` requires every gate**: `spike_ratio` ≥ 2, `asymmetry` ≥ 0.70,
`severity` ≥ 0.35, window notional ≥ $100k and ≥ 1h of baseline history.
`suppressed_by` names whichever blocked it. The two absolute floors exist
because notional is only 20% of the severity weight — without them a
perfectly one-sided window scores 0.80 on any size at all, which in
production raised alerts on $760 of liquidations. They gate the alert, not
the scoring, so `include_quiet=true` still returns the row with the reason.

The free tier is scoped to BTC; full-universe coverage is Pro and Pro Plus.

it on EVERY call from the 2026-07-24 CoinGlass retirement until 2026-08-22,
because the free-source cutover left the slot unsourced on the assumption

Full daily snapshot of all current (non-history) data in one response.

Excludes Binance spot prices and Hyperliquid data which are available
via dedicated ``/daily/prices`` and ``/daily/hyperliquid`` endpoints.

**Market health block (`market_health`)**

Dual-score architecture: 4 long-term components (Price Trend, Market Breadth,
Stablecoin Flow 90d, Macro/DXY) + 7 short-term components (Volume Quality,
Fear & Greed, Derivatives, Market Breadth Short, Volatility, Short-Term Price,
Stablecoin Flow 14d). Combined score = 0.5·LT + 0.5·ST.

- `market_health.total_score` / `long_term_score` / `short_term_score`: int 0–100
- `market_health.sentiment` / `long_term_sentiment` / `short_term_sentiment`: BULLISH | NEUTRAL | BEARISH
- `market_health.components`: `{name: {score, weight}}` (per-component details
  are stripped from `/daily`; hit `/market-health` for component `.details`)
- `market_health.indicators`: flat denormalization for quick consumption (below)

**`market_health.indicators` contract**

A flat dict of the most-filtered values from `components.<x>.details`. Keys are
**omitted entirely** when the source value is unavailable (never null) so consumers
can safely use `dict.get(key, default)` for fallbacks. Committed key set:

- `long_short_ratio` (float) — BTC long/short ratio (Binance perps)
- `funding_rate` (float, %) — avg funding rate (aliased from `avg_funding_rate`;
  CoinGlass cross-exchange when available, Binance fallback)
- `buy_ratio` (float, 0–1) — weighted taker-buy ratio across top spot pairs
- `fear_greed_value` (int, 0–100) — averaged Fear & Greed index
- `breadth_pct` (float, %) — share of top-30 coins above their 200D MA
- `pct_from_200ma` (float, %) — BTC distance from 200D MA
- `cross_status` (str) — Golden | Death | Neutral
- `stablecoin_change_7d` (float) — 7-day stablecoin market-cap change

**Cross-exchange scope**

`market_health` is computed cross-exchange (CoinGlass aggregate + Binance) and
is **not** scoped by the `exchange` query param. The `exchange` filter only
trims the `coins`, `coinglass.funding`, and `coinglass.liquidations` lists.
In particular `indicators.long_short_ratio` is BTC-on-Binance, used as a
market-wide sentiment signal — not a per-exchange Hyperliquid metric.

**Payload trimming and filter-source readiness**

To keep responses small, `coinglass.funding` and `coinglass.liquidations` are
always capped at the top 100 entries (sorted by max absolute funding rate
and 24h liquidation USD respectively) regardless of the `exchange` filter.
The full long tail is available at the dedicated
`/market-intelligence/funding-rates` and `/market-intelligence/liquidations`
endpoints. When `exchange` is set to a specific venue whose coin set has
not yet loaded after server start, this endpoint returns `503` rather than
silently emitting the unfiltered payload.

**Technical / Structural regime block (`technical_regime`)**

Universe-wide counts (`above_200ma`, `in_squeeze`, `overbought_1d`, …) plus
top-N symbol lists (`top_in_squeeze`, `top_overbought`, `top_oversold`,
`top_near_high`, `top_near_low`) as a macro overlay. The full per-symbol map
(`by_symbol`, keyed by ticker, each entry carrying the `ma` / `bollinger` /
`range_state` / `rsi` blocks) is **omitted by default** to keep this payload
compact — pass `technical_detail=true` to include it here, or read it
point-in-time from `/backtesting/daily-snapshots/{date}` where it is always
present. Per-symbol `rsi.*_1h` fields are only meaningful in the live
snapshot; backfilled historical days have no intraday series.

**Volatility regime block (`volatility_regime`)**

Realized-vol risk-sizing overlay (Regime #13): regime counts + shares
(`compressed`, `expanding`, `vol_shock`, `mean_reverting`, `normal`), a
0-100 `composite_score` (higher = more market-wide vol stress) with
`sentiment`, `median_vol_pctile_30`, and top-N lists (`top_compressed`,
`top_vol_shock`, `top_expanding`). The full per-symbol map (`by_symbol`,
each entry carrying the `regime` + `vol` metrics incl. the vol-target
multiplier) is **omitted by default** — pass `volatility_detail=true` to
include it, or read it point-in-time from `/backtesting/daily-snapshots/
{date}`. Per-symbol `vol.rv_1h` is live-only; backfilled days land null.

**SIGNUM_RGG directional trend radar (`signum_rgg`)**

Daily RED/GREY/GREEN trend classifier (ADX(14)+DMI with hysteresis) across the
full HL-perp ∪ top-Binance-spot universe — Regime #14's directional companion.
Universe summary: `green`/`grey`/`red` counts + shares, a directional
`net_breadth_pct` = (green−red)/n·100, `mean_trend_score`, a
BULLISH/NEUTRAL/BEARISH `sentiment`, and `top_green`/`top_red` (most strongly
trending). The full per-symbol map (`by_symbol`, keyed by bare ticker, each
carrying `color`, a signed `score` (+ADX green / −ADX red / 0 grey),
`adx`/`plus_di`/`minus_di`, `days_in_color`, and the `hl_symbol` join key) is
**omitted by default** — pass `signum_detail=true` to include it, or read it
point-in-time from `/backtesting/daily-snapshots/{date}`. Per-symbol
`intraday_*` are live-only; backfilled historical days land null.

Hyperliquid perpetuals: prices, funding rates, and open interest (~230 assets).

Each entry in ``funding_oi`` contains both raw and derived fields:

- ``funding_rate`` — Hyperliquid's own funding rate, per HL funding interval
  (1h on HL by default). Negative values indicate shorts paying longs.
  This is **Hyperliquid-specific**; cross-exchange averaged funding
  lives in ``/market-health`` and ``/market-intelligence/funding-rates``.
- ``open_interest`` — **in base-coin units** (number of contracts), mirroring
  the Hyperliquid API. For BTC this might be ``28846.42`` meaning ~28.8K BTC.
  Use this when comparing across exchanges that quote OI in the same units.
- ``open_interest_usd`` — derived notional in USD = ``open_interest * mark_price``.
  Use this for "is this market large enough to trade?" thresholds.
- ``mark_price`` / ``oracle_price`` — both USD.
- ``day_ntl_vlm`` — 24h notional volume, **already USD-denominated**.

- ``premium`` — Hyperliquid's own ``premium`` context field (mark vs oracle
  premium), passed through unchanged.
- ``as_of`` — ms timestamp of the ``metaAndAssetCtxs`` snapshot the row came
  from (one call covers the whole universe, so every row shares it).

Top level: ``generated_at`` (ms, when this payload was assembled),
``prices_as_of`` / ``funding_oi_as_of`` (ms fetch instants of the two HL
snapshots) and ``coverage`` = ``{universe_total, delisted_excluded, rows}``
— HL keeps delisted perps in its universe with a mark but no OI/funding, and
they are excluded here, which is why ``rows`` (~177) is below the ~232
universe. Refresh cadence: 1 minute. Thinly-traded perps may emit
``open_interest = 0`` legitimately when no positions are open.

earlier can exist; older settled funding alone is ``/backtesting/funding?

prints are archived. Window ≤ 93 days per call. Pro Plus.

The backtestable form of ``/api/v1/news/market-moving``: every qualified
catalyst with its ``impact_score``, signed ``bias``, ``corroboration``, and

Response columns are NULL for windows that have not matured yet, which means
"not yet measured", not "no reaction". Pro Plus.

get.description:
BTC miner pool reserves + 24h/7d/30d net flow per pool.

Tracks reward addresses for Foundry USA, AntPool, F2Pool, ViaBTC, and
Binance Pool. Most pools sweep balances immediately (low standing balance
is normal); the meaningful signal is the cumulative funded/spent delta
over rolling windows.

Net flow interpretation:
- **Negative net** (heavy spending): miners selling — bearish pressure
- **Positive net** (accumulation): miners holding — historically late-bear
- Windows show as `available: false` until enough snapshots have accrued

Hash Ribbon indicator: 30dMA vs 60dMA of BTC hashrate.

States:
- **capitulation**: 30dMA < 60dMA — miners shutting off rigs
- **recovery**: 30dMA just crossed back above 60dMA (within 14d) —
  historically the strongest BTC bottom signal
- **normal**: standard configuration with no recent crossover

Source: mempool.space hashrate index (3y daily history).

BTC supply-shock / dormancy signals via CoinMetrics Community API.

Returns:
- **MVRV** (market cap / realized cap) — the canonical supply-shock indicator
  with zone classification (capitulation → accumulation → neutral →
  elevated → euphoria)
- **Active addresses** — network health + adoption proxy
- **Issuance USD/24h** — direct miner pressure proxy
- **Exchange net flow USD/24h** — independent cross-check of QuickNode
  derived ERC-20 flows

Composite 0-100 on-chain health score with per-component breakdown.

Synthesizes Hash Ribbon, MVRV, stablecoin dry-powder, whale accumulation,
exchange flow direction, and miner net flow into a single directional read.

Sentiment bands:
- **bullish** (≥70): broad on-chain confluence of accumulation signals
- **leaning_bullish** (55-69): tilted positive but mixed
- **neutral** (45-54)
- **leaning_bearish** (30-44)
- **bearish** (<30): broad distribution + miner stress + flow into CEXs

Kept separate from `/market-health` for v1. Components with no data yet are
EXCLUDED and the remaining weights renormalised, so a partially-warm deploy
reports the confluence it can actually see instead of being diluted toward a
confident-looking 50. When no component has data, `sentiment` is `unknown`.

`whale_accumulation` is currently always unavailable (whale tracking is
disabled, see `/on-chain/whales`): it reports `reason: "no_data"`, its
`score` of 50 is a placeholder and it carries weight 0, so it does not move
the composite. `exchange_flow` scores the USDT/USDC/DAI 24h net only; before
2026-10-08 it also summed other tokens in their native units, so its
`reason` magnitudes from then are not dollars.

Archived CEX inflow/outflow for `symbol`, back to 2026-05-28.

The rolling windows on `/exchange-flows/{symbol}` have been sampled every
~30 minutes since 2026-05-28. Each point is one sample: the trailing 1h and
24h inflow/outflow/net summed across chains (and exchanges, unless
`exchange` is given), plus the 1h window per exchange. `interval=1h` keeps
the last sample in each UTC hour; `raw` returns every sample (their 1h
windows overlap). At most 93 days per request.

Amounts are in the token's own units (USD only for USDT/USDC/DAI) — the same
units as the live endpoint.

get.description:
Per-coin news feature series — `news_pressure` and signed `news_tilt`.

The endpoint built for trading strategies: one row per Hyperliquid perp,
cross-sectionally ranked, joinable straight onto price.

- `news_pressure` (0..1) — recency-weighted sum of impact scores, saturating.
- `news_tilt` (-1..+1) — impact-weighted direction. Negative is risk-off.
- `event_count` / `top_impact` — how much of the pressure is one big story
  versus a steady drip.

- `headlines` — raw coverage: how many stories in the current feed window
  name this coin at high confidence, whether or not any of them qualified as
  a catalyst. This is attention, not an event. The catalyst funnel discards
  ~95% of what it reads, so most coins sit at `news_pressure: 0` while
  `headlines` keeps counting; a coin high on headlines with no pressure is
  being talked about without anything happening.

**Every active perp gets a row.** A coin with no news is `news_pressure: 0`,
not a missing row — a cross-sectional ranking needs the zeros, and a silently
absent symbol is indistinguishable from a pipeline failure. Rows are ranked
by pressure first, then by `headlines`. Free tier gets the top 10 rows; Pro
and above get the full universe.

QuantProbabilityObject.description:
Full probability object for one scope (market or coin) at one horizon.

`probabilities` maps head name (directional, volatility, liquidation_risk,
funding, breadth [market only], open_interest, regime_transitions) to its
bucket->probability map; every head carries its own `confidence`.
`regime`/`probabilities` are null while the scope is warming up.

`regime` is the nowcast (present state), not a per-horizon forecast — it is
computed once and is therefore byte-identical across `horizon` values for
the same scope at the same instant. `current` is an unambiguous alias for
the same object, added so callers don't have to infer that from re-reading
`regime` at two horizons; the horizon-specific forecast lives in
`probabilities.regime_transitions` and `tomorrow`.

RawClassification.title: RawClassification
RawClassification.description:
What the cascade classifies RIGHT NOW, before the anti-churn dwell gate.

The published regime is the COMMITTED one, which by design lags the live
inputs — so ``signals`` can stop meeting the committed regime's entry
condition while that regime is still served. Without this block that reads
as contradictory data: a consumer sees ``rationale`` saying "a security
shock is active" next to a ``security_stress`` below the trigger, with no
way to tell the difference between "stale by design" and "broken".

``matches_committed`` false is normal and expected — it means a turn is
being evaluated; read ``pending.count``/``needed`` for how far along it is.

coverage_start.description: Earliest archived snapshot. A `from` earlier than this returns nothing for the uncovered part.

raw_agreement.description: Fraction of the last raw_samples ungated classifications that matched the committed regime. Decays smoothly as conditions drift, well before any candidate confirms.

RegimeStability.title: RegimeStability
RegimeStability.description:
How firmly the committed regime is holding — always present, always numeric.

``pending`` is null exactly when the live cascade agrees with the committed
regime, so a consumer polling for "is a turn brewing" gets a field that
blinks in and out of existence and carries no signal on a hold. This block
is the continuous companion: it is emitted on every response, candidate or
not, so it can be differenced, thresholded, or fed to a risk sizer directly.

``locked_for_s`` is the only HARD number here — the minimum-dwell floor
mechanically prevents any change for that long. The one exception is a
Structural Shock override, which is exempt from the floor by design.
